[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "route (Old French rute, from Latin rupta via) = broken way; harvest (Old English hærfest) = autumn, reaping time",
    "reading": "A broken path through the season of reaping; the way that is cut, then gathered.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "la", "ang"],
    "source": "OED: route from rupta (via); harvest from hærfest",
    "confidence": 0.8
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Route = root (homophone) + 91 = nine-one; Harvest = har + vest; har (Old Norse) = grey, vest = garment",
    "reading": "The root of nine-one: a grey garment worn at the gathering, the hidden core of the count.",
    "languages": ["en", "non"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Route (fr. route) = road; Harvest (fr. récolte) but 'harvest' sounds like 'har veste' (fr. har = no, veste = jacket) — 'no jacket'",
    "reading": "On the road without a jacket — the stripping of cover at the time of reaping.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Route 91 Harvest -> 'Vesture, a hot rar' (anagram) — vesture = clothing, rar = rare, hot = heat",
    "reading": "Rare heat becomes clothing; the harvest wraps itself in the warmth of the day.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "R = Re, 9 = I, 1 = A, H = H, V = V — R9H1V; read as 'Re' (again) + 'I' (self) + 'A' (first) + 'H' (breath) + 'V' (life)",
    "reading": "Again the self, first breath, life — the cycle of return in the reaping.",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "R = the road (Latin rota, wheel); 9 = the ninth letter, I (self); 1 = A (beginning); H = breath (spiritus); V = victory (Latin victoria)",
    "reading": "Wheel of self, beginning of breath, victory — the harvest as a turning point of spirit.",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "Route = 5 letters, 91 = 9+1=10, Harvest = 7 letters; 5+10+7=22; 22 = the Fool (tarot) or Hebrew letter Tav (cross, seal)",
    "reading": "The sum is twenty-two: the seal of completion, the fool's journey through the reaped field.",
    "languages": ["en", "he"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Harvest from Proto-Germanic *harbistaz = autumn; related to Old English herfest, also 'to pluck' (Latin carpere)",
    "reading": "The plucking-time; the season when the road is broken by the act of taking what is ripe.",
    "languages": ["en", "gem", "la"],
    "source": "Klein's Comprehensive Etymological Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.7
  }
]
